subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should later global `tools.exec` security config override persisted per-session `/exec` fields, and how should existing persisted session entries be migrated or reset?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes a documented session-state and exec security precedence contract, so automation should not choose the permanent security boundary alone.

options.title: Make operator config authoritative
options.body: Update precedence or migration/reset behavior so stricter global exec policy takes effect for existing sessions while preserving only explicitly approved safe session state.

options.title: Keep `/exec` session defaults sticky
options.body: Treat current behavior as intentional, but document the security tradeoff and provide an operator-visible way to clear stale exec session fields.

options.title: Require an explicit reset or doctor path first
options.body: Keep resolver behavior unchanged until a tested session cleanup or doctor migration can safely handle existing stored entries.

recommendation.title: Make operator config authoritative
recommendation.body: Update precedence or migration/reset behavior so stricter global exec policy takes effect for existing sessions while preserving only explicitly approved safe session state.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced `/exec` session overrides and later owned directive persistence gating, making them the best routing candidate for the security-precedence decision.
